pattern_explanation: Both languages borrowed many medical and everyday words from the same Latin and Greek roots, so the spellings of these words look alike. Over time, the meanings drifted apart in each language, so the look-alike form often carries a different meaning in English.
false_friend_warning: Learners may think the Portuguese word that looks like 'constipation' means constipation in English, because the spellings are close. In English, that word describes a common cold, while 'constipation' refers to a problem with the bowels. Also, the Portuguese word that looks like 'academy' means gym in everyday English.
